lineup: Hour 1 is all college football - the Week 3 reset and new poll, West Virginia, and picks for the biggest games on today's Week 4 board. Hour 2 opens live from Knoxville with Michael Patrick Leahy on scene for Texas at Tennessee, then five minutes of fantasy with Trent Conner, then NFL Week 3 - Thursday night, the Week 2 rewind, Sunday and primetime picks, and a lock of the week from each panelist.
lines_note: NFL spreads and totals from DraftKings via CBS Sports, captured Friday 9/25 at 11:12 AM ET. College football lines from FanDuel via SportsGrid, captured 9/25. Lines will move before kickoff.
verify: Michael Patrick Leahy's live hit at 10:00 ET from Knoxville - confirm the connection and his location before air, and have a backup topic ready if the shot drops.

Fantasy segment: Denzel Boston's exact Week 2 line and roster percentage (sources conflict), Keon Coleman's ankle (listed as a top add by one outlet, out by another), and Travis Etienne's team label (sources list both New Orleans and Jacksonville).
Giants' starting QB with Jaxson Dart out for the season - Yahoo reports Jameis Winston, other reports mention Russell Wilson. Check the Friday depth chart before naming him.
Atlanta and Green Bay records after Thursday night. We have both at 1-2; confirm on the NFL standings page.
Caleb Williams (hamstring) and Tyson Bagent (concussion protocol) for Monday night. Case Keenum is the fallback.
Friday NFL designations: Puka Nacua (hip), Zay Flowers (hamstring), Nico Collins (hamstring), DJ Moore (shoulder), Brock Bowers (knee), Sam Darnold.
Oregon's ranking - the AP poll has them 20th, some slate pages list 21st.
Week number for the college slate - most outlets call today Week 4, one calls it Week 5. Say Week 4.
Iowa-Michigan and Oklahoma-Georgia spreads differ by about a point between FanDuel and DraftKings/CBS.
No Oklahoma State injury report confirmed for the WVU game - check Friday's release before listing anyone.
Ohio State's one loss is reported as the Texas comeback but we did not confirm that game's box score. Don't cite a score.
Home team on the Rio game - it is a neutral site and sources label it both ways. Pick one and stay consistent.
Re-pull all NFL and college lines Saturday morning and say which book on air.

hours.title: Hour 1
hours.subtitle: College Football - Week 3 reset, West Virginia, and Week 4 picks

blocks.title: Block 1: Week 3 Reset and the New Poll

items.h: Texas still No. 1, Ole Miss jumps to No. 4
items.t: AP Top 10: 1 Texas (3-0), 2 Georgia (3-0), 3 Notre Dame (3-0), 4 Ole Miss (3-0), 5 Indiana (3-0), 6 Miami (3-0), 7 Ohio State (2-1), 8 Alabama (3-0), 9 BYU (3-0), 10 LSU (2-1).

items.h: 11 through 25
items.t: Texas Tech, USC (4-0), Penn State, Tennessee, Utah, Louisville, Iowa, Michigan, Missouri, Oregon, Florida, SMU, Texas A&M, Mississippi State, Houston.

items.h: Biggest movers
items.t: Ole Miss into the top five. Texas A&M down 15 spots to 23 after losing at home. SMU down six after losing to Louisville, which climbed to 16. Michigan back at 18.

items.h: Ole Miss 32, LSU 24
items.t: Trinidad Chambliss went 33-of-48 for 363 yards and three total touchdowns in Oxford. Traylon Ray had 7 catches for 115 and a score, and Ole Miss outgained LSU 426-330. The Rebels are the only team in the country with two wins over ranked opponents.

items.h: Around the country
items.t: Alabama 50 Florida State 36, Georgia 45 Arkansas 17, Florida 44 Auburn 39, Notre Dame 27 Michigan State 10, Ohio State 59 Kent State 3, Iowa 55 Northern Iowa 0.

items.h: Kentucky 31, Texas A&M 21 - upset of the week
items.t: Unranked Kentucky walked into College Station and beat the then-No. 9 Aggies, who fell 15 spots in the poll.

items.h: How Kentucky pulled it off
items.t: Full recap of the Wildcats' win in College Station.

items.h: Two ranked teams went down on the same day
items.t: Kentucky and West Virginia both knocked off top-25 opponents in Week 3.

items.h: Hawkins accounted for all five touchdowns
items.t: Michael Hawkins Jr. put up 313 total yards - 10-of-17 for 190 and two scores through the air, 18 carries for 123 and three on the ground. He was named Big 12 Offensive Player of the Week.

items.h: This was a neutral site, not a road game
items.t: The Duke's Mayo Classic at Bank of America Stadium in Charlotte. Roughly two-thirds of the 39,377 in the building wore gold.

items.h: 3-0 for the first time since 2018
items.t: The Mountaineers are receiving AP votes but have not cracked the poll.

segments.title: Today: Oklahoma State at West Virginia

items.h: 7:00 PM ET on FS1, Gold Rush game in Morgantown
items.t: West Virginia -1.5, total 61.5. Moneyline WVU -122, Oklahoma State +102 (FanDuel, captured 9/25).

items.h: Two of the best offenses in the league
items.t: Both teams average better than 35 points a game. Oklahoma State leads the Big 12 in total offense at 528.0 yards and passing at 306.3; West Virginia leads it in rushing at 281.3 behind Hawkins and Cam Cook. Cowboys QB Drew Mestemaker went 20-of-22 for 324 and five scores against Murray State.

items.h: Oklahoma State is carrying two long losing streaks
items.t: Eighteen straight Big 12 losses and eleven straight on the road, their longest road skid since the 1930s - but they already own an upset of Oregon this season.

items.h: WVU injury news is mostly good
items.t: Rich Rodriguez says LG Nick Krahe will be limited in practice but should play. WR Jaden Bray (hip bruise), TE Cam Ball and RBs Martavious Boswell and Talley are all expected to go, and WR Prince Strachan gets an expanded role after a full week.

items.h: Talker for the segment
items.t: Big 12 opener, a one-and-a-half point line and a 61.5 total. Is this the week WVU gets into the poll, or is Oklahoma State the trap?

items.h: Noon ET on ABC, Texas -4.5, total 54.5
items.t: The top-ranked team on the road in the loudest building on the schedule. Michael Patrick Leahy is on scene for this one and joins us live at 10:00 in Hour 2.

items.h: Arch Manning has never been to Knoxville
items.t: Manning has 664 yards, 7 TD and 2 INT, including a 20-point comeback against Ohio State. Tennessee counters with freshman Faizon Brandon at 552 yards and 6 TD. Vols RB DeSean Bishop (hip) left the Kennesaw State game twice but is expected to play. Steve Sarkisian: "I just had assumed he'd been to Knoxville. He's never been before."

segments.title: No. 4 Ole Miss at No. 21 Florida

items.h: 3:30 PM ET on ABC, Florida -3.5, total 58.5
items.t: A top-five team getting points on the road - the best ranked-versus-ranked number on the board. Moneyline Ole Miss +130.

items.h: Florida is coming off a 44-39 win over Auburn
items.t: Ole Miss has beaten two ranked teams already; the Gators just came out of a shootout.

items.h: 7:30 PM ET on NBC, Oregon -2.5, total 61.5
items.t: Road favorite against a 4-0 USC team riding a 10-game home winning streak, and the highest total of the marquee games.

items.h: USC's injury list is long
items.t: Out: WR Corey Simms, S Kendarius Reddick, LB Taylor Johnson, OL Kilian O'Connor. Doubtful: WR Trent Mosley. Questionable: DT Jahkeem Stewart, RB Deshonne Redeaux, S Alex Graham, LB Jadyn Walker.

items.h: Oregon's receiver room is banged up too
items.t: Out: WR Jeremiah McClellan (broken foot), OL Trent Ferguson (knee, season), ILB Brayden Platt, RB Simeon Price. WR Jalen Lott is doubtful - Dan Lanning: "I don't know that you'll see him in this game."

items.h: 3:30 PM ET on CBS, Michigan -5.5, total 38.5
items.t: The lowest total on the board by a wide margin. DraftKings has it at Michigan -4.5 and 37.5 - a full point of difference, so say which book.

items.h: Iowa is getting bodies back
items.t: TE DJ Vonnahme missed the Northern Iowa game but Kirk Ferentz is optimistic, and RBs Kamari Moulton and LJ Phillips are expected available.

items.h: No. 23 Texas A&M at No. 10 LSU, 7:30 PM ET on ABC
items.t: LSU -9.5, total 52.5. Both teams are 2-1 and coming off losses; the loser is in real trouble.

items.h: Oklahoma at No. 2 Georgia, 3:30 PM ET on ESPN
items.t: Georgia -12.5 and 44.5 at FanDuel, Georgia -14 and 43.5 at CBS. Georgia is averaging 59.3 points and nobody has come within 32. CBS reports friction between Oklahoma QB John Mateer and OC Ben Arbuckle, and Georgia RB Nate Frazier (ankle) is expected to play.

items.h: Illinois at No. 7 Ohio State, Noon on FOX
items.t: Ohio State -27.5, total 53.5. All three Illinois tight ends are out for the season along with WR Alex Perry and OG Brandon Henderson. Ohio State has won 10 straight in the series.

items.h: Also worth a mention
items.t: No. 19 Missouri at No. 24 Mississippi State, 7:30 on SEC Network. Wake Forest at No. 16 Louisville, Noon on ESPN.

items.h: Full Week 4 grid
items.t: Every matchup, kickoff time and network for today.

hours.title: Hour 2
hours.subtitle: Live from Knoxville with Michael Patrick Leahy, five minutes of fantasy with Trent Conner, then NFL Week 3

blocks.title: Block 1: Live from Knoxville - Michael Patrick Leahy

segments.title: LIVE HIT: Michael Patrick Leahy on scene at Neyland

items.h: Leahy joins at 10:00 ET, on site for Texas at Tennessee
items.t: Hard start at the top of the hour. Set him up with where he is and how long until kickoff - the game goes at Noon ET on ABC, so he is about two hours out when we come to him.

items.h: The game he is there for
items.t: No. 1 Texas at No. 14 Tennessee. Texas -4.5, total 54.5 (FanDuel, captured 9/25). The top-ranked team on the road in the loudest building on the schedule.

items.h: Questions for Leahy
items.t: What does the campus feel like this morning? How is Knoxville treating the Arch Manning storyline - is it a Peyton thing or a Texas thing? Weather and field conditions. Any early word on DeSean Bishop (hip). What is the crowd expecting from freshman Faizon Brandon?

items.h: Background for the conversation
items.t: Manning has 664 yards, 7 TD and 2 INT and has never been to Knoxville. Brandon is at 552 yards and 6 TD. Sarkisian: "I just had assumed he'd been to Knoxville. He's never been before."

items.h: Panel reaction
items.t: Quick round on what Leahy told us and whether it changes anybody's read on the game or the number.

items.h: Handoff
items.t: Thank Leahy, tell listeners where to follow him for the rest of the day, and go to Trent for the fantasy five.

blocks.title: Block 2: Five Minutes of Fantasy with Trent Conner

items.h: Start of the week: David Montgomery (HOU) vs IND
items.t: The Colts are bottom-three in rush yards over expected and success rate and have allowed nine red zone trips. Montgomery also got the two-minute work in Week 2.

items.h: Tight end start: Dalton Kincaid (BUF) vs LAC
items.t: He leads Buffalo in routes, targets, catches and receiving yards. Mark Andrews vs DAL is the other one - Dallas allows the third-most fantasy points per target to tight ends.

items.h: Sit of the week: Travis Etienne vs LV
items.t: Alvin Kamara's return tanked his usage - two targets in Week 2. Also sit Colston Loveland against an Eagles defense allowing a league-low 10.2 fantasy points to tight ends.

items.h: Waiver add: Denzel Boston (CLE)
items.t: The top overall add - 21.2 percent target share, a 95 percent route rate and eighth in the NFL in red zone targets. About 33 percent rostered, worth roughly 10 percent FAAB.

items.h: Stash before he breaks out: Rashod Bateman (BAL)
items.t: Seven catches on nine targets for 88 yards with Zay Flowers out, and Baltimore has the highest implied total on the board in Rio. Cheap streamer if you need one: Drew Lock at 7 percent rostered against a Washington defense that allows the most passing scores in the league.

items.h: Keep it to five
items.t: Hard out at 10:17 - one line per name, Trent picks the order.

items.h: Atlanta scored 27 straight at Lambeau
items.t: The Falcons fell behind 7-0 and never trailed again. Bijan Robinson ran for 194 and two touchdowns as part of 242 team rushing yards, and Drake London caught 9 for 194 - the first time since 1976 that two road teammates each had 190-plus scrimmage yards.

items.h: Penix looked like himself in his return
items.t: Michael Penix Jr., back from a November ACL tear, went 18-of-25 for 256 with a touchdown and a pick.

items.h: Green Bay could not run it at all
items.t: Jordan Love threw 53 times for 312 yards and two scores while the Packers rushed eight times for 17 yards. It is their first home-opener loss since 2012, ending a 13-game streak.

items.h: Thursday injuries
items.t: Falcons CB A.J. Terrell went on injured reserve with a groin injury. Packers LB Edgerrin Cooper was evaluated for a concussion and G Jacob Monk hurt a quad. Green Bay was already without Jayden Reed (neck) and Aaron Banks (knee/toe).

items.h: Biggest upset: Raiders 26, Chargers 14
items.t: Kirk Cousins went 8-of-12 for 181 yards and three touchdowns on throws of 10-plus air yards. Las Vegas is 2-0, the Chargers 0-2.

items.h: Mahomes went vintage in overtime
items.t: 382 yards and three touchdowns with a career-high 14 play-action completions in a 33-30 OT win over Indianapolis.

items.h: It was a defense week
items.t: Vikings 9, Bears 3 with Brian Flores blitzing Caleb Williams on 81.8 percent of dropbacks. Carolina beat Atlanta 34-3 behind Devin Lloyd's sack, two interceptions and a pick-six. Five defenses allowed no touchdowns and New England held Pittsburgh to three.

items.h: Dak passed Romo
items.t: Four touchdown passes against Washington moved Dak Prescott past Tony Romo for the Cowboys career record in a 37-20 win.

items.h: Full Week 2 scoreboard
items.t: Every score, including Rams 28, Giants 6 on Monday night.

items.h: How we are handling the numbers
items.t: Every spread and total this hour is DraftKings via CBS Sports, captured Friday morning at 11:12 ET. Sixteen games, no byes.

items.h: The extremes
items.t: Highest total on the board is Ravens-Cowboys in Rio at 52.5, four points clear of anything else. Lowest are Seahawks-Commanders and Titans-Giants at 40.5. Biggest spread is Kansas City -11.5 in Miami.

items.h: Full schedule and kickoff times
items.t: Every Week 3 game with its window and network.

segments.title: Ravens vs Cowboys in Rio de Janeiro

items.h: 4:25 PM ET on CBS, Baltimore -3, total 52.5
items.t: The NFL's first game in Rio and the highest total of the week by four points.

items.h: Both sides are shorthanded
items.t: Zay Flowers did not practice with a hamstring and is trending toward missing it. Dallas is out LB DeMarvion Overshown, CB Cobie Durant, S Malik Hooker and S P.J. Locke - a shredded secondary against Lamar Jackson.

items.h: The angle
items.t: Baltimore lost to New Orleans and is fighting off 0-2 talk; Dak is coming off a franchise-record night. A 52.5 with a depleted Dallas secondary is the number to talk about.

items.h: 1:00 PM ET on FOX, Seattle -7, total 40.5
items.t: The lowest total on the board, and a seven-point road favorite.

items.h: Seattle is on a franchise-record 12-game winning streak
items.t: Counting the playoffs. Drew Lock has a 127.3 rating, zero turnovers and four touchdown passes - all four to Jaxon Smith-Njigba, who is on pace to be only the second player ever with 120-plus receiving yards and a touchdown in each of his team's first three games. Sam Darnold returned to practice Wednesday and is day-to-day.

items.h: Washington is starting Marcus Mariota
items.t: Jayden Daniels is out indefinitely with a dislocated elbow and is seeking additional opinions. The Commanders are 0-2.

segments.title: Chiefs at Dolphins and Bengals at Steelers

items.h: Chiefs at Dolphins, 1:00 PM ET on CBS
items.t: Kansas City -11.5, total 46 - the biggest spread of the week. Mahomes is coming off the 382-yard overtime win, Miami off a 35-13 beating in San Francisco.

items.h: Bengals at Steelers, 1:00 PM ET on CBS
items.t: Cincinnati -3.5, total 42.5. The Bengals are 2-0 and held Houston to six points; Pittsburgh scored three in New England. A rare road favorite in this rivalry.

items.h: Chargers at Bills, 1:00 PM ET on FOX
items.t: Buffalo -7, total 46. Los Angeles is 0-2 after losing to the Raiders; Buffalo hung 41 on Detroit. Bills WR DJ Moore (shoulder) is day-to-day and the Chargers are down two tight ends.

items.h: Titans at Giants, 1:00 PM ET on CBS
items.t: New York -3, total 40.5, with the quarterback situation unsettled - the live number of the early window.

items.h: Jaxson Dart is out for the season
items.t: Torn MCL in the Monday night loss to the Rams, followed by knee surgery.

items.h: The rest of the card
items.t: Patriots at Jaguars JAX -3 / 45.5. Texans at Colts HOU -2.5 / 43.5. Jets at Lions DET -6.5 / 48. Panthers at Browns CAR -2.5 / 42.5. Vikings at Buccaneers MIN -1.5 / 42.5. Cardinals at 49ers SF -8.5 / 47.5. Raiders at Saints NO -3 / 43.5, with Brock Bowers close to returning.

items.h: 8:20 PM ET on NBC, Rams -2.5, total 45.5
items.t: The tightest primetime line of the weekend.

items.h: Puka Nacua is likely out again
items.t: Sean McVay said Nacua is not making great progress on the hip. Denver is coming off a win over Jacksonville.

items.h: 8:15 PM ET on ABC and ESPN, Eagles -3.5, total 43.5
items.t: Monday night in Chicago.

items.h: Chicago may be down to its third quarterback
items.t: Caleb Williams (hamstring) did not practice all week and is week to week; backup Tyson Bagent is in concussion protocol. Fourteen-year veteran Case Keenum is next in line.

items.h: Philadelphia's report is ugly too
items.t: DNPs for TE Dallas Goedert (MCL sprain, multiple weeks), WR DeVonta Smith (hamstring), RB Tank Bigsby and RB Will Shipley. Saquon Barkley was limited with a stinger. Chicago is also without K Cairo Santos, RB Kyle Monangai and CB Tyrique Stevenson.

segments.title: Lock of the week and close

items.h: Lock of the week from each panelist
items.t: Around the table - one play, one sentence of reasoning, on the record. No repeats.

items.h: Close
items.t: Reset the primetime schedule - Rams at Broncos Sunday night on NBC, Eagles at Bears Monday night on ABC and ESPN, and the Rio game at 4:25 on CBS. Tease next week.
